findings.problem: LeaseWorkflow uses String for status and bool flags (is_validated, is_sent) instead of domain enums or typestates. This makes illegal states representable - e.g. status=sent with is_sent=false, or status=sent with is_validated=false.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct LeaseWorkflow with contradictory status/flag combinations, enabling workflows that violate domain invariants such as marking a lease as sent before validation or having ambiguous intermediate states.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a sealed enum LeaseStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }. Replace is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool with the enum - the status enum encodes the full lifecycle. Use a typed constructor that only allows valid transitions.

findings.problem: id: String is an unvalidated primitive. Domain IDs should be represented as a newtype (e.g. LeaseId(String)) with a fallible constructor that enforces format/length rules at the boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, malformed IDs, or non-lease-IDs can flow through the system, causing silent logical errors or downstream failures. No parsing/validation boundary is enforced.
findings.fix: Introduce pub struct LeaseId(String) with fn new(s: String) -> Result<LeaseId, LeaseError> and use LeaseId in the struct instead of String.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates LeaseWorkflow in place with direct field assignment (item.status = "sent".to_string()). This is imperative mutation inside the core with no validation, no domain error, and no typestate guard.
findings.failure_mode: The function can be called on any LeaseWorkflow regardless of its current state, allowing transitions like Pending to Sent skipping Validated. No invariant checking occurs.
findings.fix: Replace with a pure function mark_sent(status: LeaseStatus) -> Result<LeaseStatus, LeaseTransitionError> that only permits Validated to Sent, returning a typed error for invalid transitions.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> stores raw epoch milliseconds without any newtype or validation. The domain may have range or monotonicity constraints on timestamps.
findings.failure_mode: Zero, negative (via overflow), or nonsensical timestamps can be stored, leading to incorrect ordering, sorting, or lease-expiry calculations.
findings.fix: Introduce pub struct SentAtEpochMs(u64) with a constructor that rejects zero and enforces domain constraints, then use it instead of Option<u64>.

findings.problem: All fields of LeaseWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate fields directly without any domain logic or validation.
findings.failure_mode: External code can bypass mark_sent and any future validation by directly assigning to item.status or item.is_sent, making all core invariants voidable.
findings.fix: Make fields private or remove the struct entirely in favor of an immutable typestate model where transitions produce new values rather than mutating existing ones.

findings.problem: status: String allows arbitrary strings (e.g. SENT, sent!, empty, cancelled, deleted) that have no meaning in the domain. String comparison is error-prone and case-sensitive.
findings.failure_mode: Typo bugs, case mismatches, and unrecognized status values cause silent failures or panics in downstream code that assumes a closed set of status values.
findings.fix: Replace with enum LeaseStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } - a closed, exhaustive set that the compiler enforces at match/transition points.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The code is fundamentally broken at the type-system level - illegal states are fully representable, the functional core is imperative mutation, and all domain invariants are voidable by external code. The codebase needs a typestate redesign before any correctness or performance claims are meaningful.
